head.title: Nocturne · Keep everything, ask about it, get one page each morning
head.description: Nocturne is a free, private app for your computer. Save notes, photos, voice notes and files without sorting them, now or later. Ask about any of it later, and each morning get one page of what needs you, with the original behind every line.
head.og.description: Save notes, photos, voice notes and files without sorting them, now or later. Ask about any of it later, and each morning get one page of what needs you, all on your own computer.
head.og.image.alt: Nocturne. Keep everything. Nocturne remembers it for you. Ask about any of it later, and get one page each morning of what needs you. Beside the words, the morning page from the app with demo data.
hero.title: Keep everything. Nocturne remembers it for you.
hero.lede: Save notes, photos, voice notes and files without sorting them, now or later. Ask about any of it later, and each morning get one page of what needs you, all on your own computer.
hero.page.alt: The morning page in Nocturne: Friday 13 November, two things need you today. The Year 4 trip form is due next Friday, with the letter it came from. The dentist appointment changed, with a choice between the card and the voice note.
hero.keep.alt: The keep box with “Gran’s new number ends 4471” typed in, and Keep and Ask buttons.
hero.caption: Keep it in one box, read it on the morning page. From the app, with demo data.
how.title: Keep it now. Read it once.
keep.title: Keep anything, file nothing.
keep.body: Press <kbd>Ctrl Shift Space</kbd>, or <kbd>Cmd Shift Space</kbd> on a Mac, then type, talk, paste or drop a photo or a PDF. Nocturne says “Kept.” and you get back to your day. No folders or tags to keep up: you ask, and it finds it. If it cannot read something, it tells you what to do.
keep.box.alt: The quick keep box with “Gran’s new number ends 4471” typed in, and Keep and Ask buttons.
keep.recent.alt: Recently kept: a photo still being read, voice notes and pasted messages marked understood, a password-locked PDF Nocturne could not read with what to do about it, and a voice note that needs you.
ask.title: Answers with receipts.
ask.body: Ask in plain words. Nocturne answers only from what you kept, with the originals underneath so you can check. When it does not know, it says so. If it gets something wrong, tell it what is right and it remembers.
ask.alt: An answer to “What does Leo need for his trip?”: a packed lunch, and the trip form is due next Friday with a signature and £12. Below it, the two photographed letters it came from.
page.eyebrow: The morning page · at your time
page.title: Wake to what needs you.
page.body: Whenever the computer is plugged in and idle, by night or by day, Nocturne reads what you kept and notices what changed. At the time you choose, you get a short list to read, hear or print. When two things disagree, it asks instead of guessing.
page.alt: The morning page: two things need you today. The Year 4 trip form is due next Friday, with the letter it came from. The dentist appointment changed, with a choice between the appointment card and the voice note.
privacy.title: Your life stays on your computer.
privacy.body: Out of the box, Nocturne goes online only for downloads you agree to: its mind at setup and any update you allow. Privacy in the app lists each one with the day and the size.
promise.signin.detail: No account, no analytics, no crash reports, no cloud copy.
promise.checked.detail: Before a release, Nocturne is run with its network cut off from everything but this computer, and any attempt to reach further fails the check.
promise.edit.term: It never edits what you kept
promise.edit.detail: Your notes, photos and files are never changed. Every answer shows them underneath. If one is wrong, tell it what is right; the old version is kept, not overwritten.
promise.forget.detail: Things you no longer use fade, and the page says when one is let go. Bring any back; forgetting for good always asks first.
promise.note.detail: When the page is ready, one note says so and how many things need you. Never what you kept.
promise.extras.term: Two extras, off until you ask
promise.extras.detail: Away from home lets your own phone ask, keep and read your page, sealed so the company in between cannot read it. Online answers sends a question, and the few remembered sentences it needs, to one service you choose. Never anything marked private.
phone.alt: Nocturne on a paired phone: connected to the home computer, with Ask, Keep and today’s page, and a note that things marked private stay on the computer.
phone.caption: Away from home on a paired phone, with demo data.
engine.title: Built on
engine.body1: Nocturne’s thinking runs on Embeddable Lemonade, the portable build of Lemonade, the open-source local AI server. Nocturne ships its own copy, Lemonade {{LEMONADE_VERSION}}, that only this computer can reach.
engine.body2: Lemonade is free under the Apache 2.0 licence and built by its community, with optimisations by AMD engineers. Nocturne would not exist without it.
req.title: Will it run on my computer?
req.body: Almost certainly, if it has 8 GB of memory: an 8 GB MacBook Air, or a typical 8 GB Windows or Linux laptop.
req.memory.detail: 8 GB is enough. On an 8 GB computer Nocturne uses about 5 GB at its busiest and gives it back when it has nothing to do. With more memory it offers a larger setup with clearer answers.
req.graphics.detail: No graphics card needed. Macs with Apple silicon, and computers with AMD or Intel graphics built in, run Nocturne on the chip and share the computer’s memory. An AMD or NVIDIA graphics card works too, best with 6 GB or more. Other computers run it on the processor.
req.chip.detail: Helpful, never needed. On some AMD computers with an AI chip and 16 GB or more, the AI chip reads your voice notes, so answers and the daily tidy do not wait for them.
req.system.detail: macOS 26 or later on an Apple chip, Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), or 64-bit Linux on Intel, AMD or Arm.
tier.large.name: Large
tier.standard.name: Standard
tier.small.name: Small
tier.small.text: Same page. The daily tidy takes longer.
tier.tiny.name: Tiny
tier.tiny.text: Made for 8 GB computers. Simpler answers that may miss details.
req.downloads: Downloads at setup are between about 3 GB and 26 GB, depending on the setup. After that, Nocturne works with no internet at all.
get.title: Get Nocturne.
get.body: Free and open source, for Mac, Windows and Linux. Download it, open it, and it sets itself up for the computer it is on.
install.title: Get Nocturne · Download for Mac, Windows and Linux
install.description: Download Nocturne for a Mac with an Apple chip, a Windows 10 or 11 computer, or a Linux desktop. Free and open source, with no account. The first time it opens, it sets itself up for the computer it is on.
install.og.description: Free and open source, with no account. The first time it opens, Nocturne sets itself up for the computer it is on.
install.heading: Get Nocturne.
install.lede: Free and open source, for Mac, Windows and Linux. No account, nothing to sign in to.
install.here: Choose your computer below. Each link gives the latest version.
mac.spec: Apple chip, M1 or later · macOS 26 or later
mac.note: Macs with an Intel chip are not supported. To see which chip yours has, open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac.
install.firstOpen: The first time you open it
mac.step1: Open the downloaded file, then drag Nocturne into Applications.
mac.step2: Open Nocturne from Applications. Your Mac says Nocturne Not Opened, because it could not check the app. Click Done.
mac.step3: Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security. Scroll down to the line saying Nocturne was blocked and click Open Anyway.
mac.step4: Enter your password, then click Open Anyway again.
mac.why: You only do this once. Apple charges a yearly fee to sign an app so it opens without asking; Nocturne is free and open source, and this release is not signed yet.
win.note: Installs for you alone and needs no administrator password. Computers managed by an organisation can use the .msi installer instead.
win.step1: Your browser may warn that the file is not commonly downloaded. In Edge, open the … menu beside the file, choose Keep, then Show more, then Keep anyway.
win.step2: Open the installer. Windows shows Windows protected your PC. Click More info, then Run anyway.
win.why: You only do this once. Microsoft charges a yearly fee to sign an app so it opens without asking; Nocturne is free and open source, and this release is not signed yet.
linux.spec: 64-bit computer with an Intel, AMD or Arm chip
linux.flatpak.title: From your software centre
linux.flatpak.text: The choice for most people, on any Linux desktop. Your software centre keeps Nocturne up to date. Starting with the computer is not available this way yet.
linux.flatpak.terminal: Or install it from a terminal
linux.deb.title: Ubuntu, Linux Mint or Debian
linux.package.text: Open the file with your software centre, and Nocturne appears with your other apps.
linux.rpm.title: Fedora, Red Hat or openSUSE
linux.appimage.title: Try it without installing
linux.appimage.text: One file that runs on most desktops. In its properties, allow it to run as a program, then open it.
linux.note: Most Linux computers have an Intel or AMD chip. To check, run uname -m in a terminal: x86_64 means Intel or AMD, aarch64 means Arm. The Flatpak picks the right one by itself.
linux.why: Linux shows no warning the first time you open Nocturne.
install.checks: To make sure a download is the one we published, compare it with the fingerprints in SHA256SUMS. The install guide{{en_mark}} shows how, explains each package and how to take Nocturne off again. Earlier versions are on the releases page.
needs.title: What your computer needs.
after.title: After you install.
after.body: Nocturne opens a short setup. You can keep things straight away.
after.1.title: It looks at the computer
after.1.text: It tells you which setup it will use. You can always pick a smaller one, which uses less memory, space and battery.
after.2.title: It downloads what it needs
after.2.text: It asks first, then downloads what this computer can run: between about 3 GB and 26 GB. This is the only time Nocturne needs the internet, and it carries on by itself if the connection drops.
after.3.title: Your first page
after.3.text: From then on, Nocturne works with no internet at all.
